thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-api request-queue length 11,200 across us-east-1 pools; p95 3.2s -> p95 7.4s, p99 1.2s -> p99 12.6s. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale ops, all failed with 'scale_limit_reached' and 'no_resource_offers'. Investigating.

oncall-rajan: I'm on it. Paging infra and SRE.

maya: I'm awake, jumping in now. can you post the autoscaler logs?

ops-bot: Autoscaler event stream (tail):
```
2026-03-14T02:01:12Z INFO desired=120 current=80 attempting_scale=40
2026-03-14T02:01:13Z ERROR launch-failed reason=quota_exceeded region=us-east-1 details="GPU quota 100, request 120"
2026-03-14T02:01:15Z WARN no_offers found for pods cpu=16 gpu=1 mem=64G
2026-03-14T02:01:18Z ERROR scale_failed reason=scale_limit_reached max_pools=3
```

oncall-rajan: Thanks. Looks like quota + scheduler couldn't find matching nodes for large-gpu flavor. Also seeing allocator returning 'opaque' on some offers.

infra-zoe: Confirmed. Cloud reports temporary shortage of the specific A100-80GB SKU in the zone. Quota itself is fine for total GPUs but regional SKU availability is zero. We're hitting our preferred pool selector which requires 80GB GPUs for big-model endpoints.

samir: Is the autoscaler unable to pick smaller instance types? We have compatible 40GB and 24GB variants — why are requests pinned to 80GB?

maya: Because model version constraints: a subset of requests are routed to model:redwood-xl-80 because clients set model_hint="xl-latency" in headers. Routing policy is strict for now.

eng-sre-lee: We're seeing many large-sequence/callers from a small set of customers causing batching to pick the 80GB path. Queue histogram: 60% of queued tokens are from 6 customers. CSM-olga, do you have names?

csm-olga: Top 6: fin-analytics (high QPS), docs-gen-pro, searchlytics, social-ai, marketplace-ai, chatinc. Fin-analytics and docs-gen-pro make up ~48% of queued requests. They started a new experiment ~01:30 UTC.

maya: Quick mitigation idea: 1) loosen routing: allow model hint fallback to compatible 40GB-quantized variant; 2) temporarily lower per-client concurrency for the top 6; 3) enable emergency soft-rate limit for anonymous/free-tier to preserve capacity for paid customers. Can we do 1) fast?

infra-zoe: I can flip a routing toggle but need a short maintenance window because it will cause ephemeral reconnects. 2) we can enforce concurrency at the gateway immediately. 3) rate limits require product sign-off but we can apply a temporary soft throttle via edge rules.

oncall-rajan: Maya — do the routing flip. Zoe — prepare the edge throttle. Lee — start draining/processing queued small requests first (priority rewrite). Olga — notify the two enterprise contacts that we're investigating and may throttle experimental traffic.

maya: executing routing change now. command:
```
curl -X PATCH https://console.internal.redwood/api/routing/policies/allow-fallback \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
 -d '{"from_model":"redwood-xl-80","allow_fallback":true,"fallback_models":["redwood-large-40-q","redwood-medium-24-q"]}'
```

maya: patch sent. traffic should start landing on quantized 40/24 variants. watching metrics.

ops-bot: Deploy notifier: routing-policy updated by maya (patch-4023).

eng-sre-lee: Metrics show initial shift: 22% of new requests routed to 40/24 within 45s. Queue length trending down to 8.3k but p99 still 9.8s. Some stuck requests still targeting 80GB lane — these are long-sequence calls that cannot be processed by smaller models without quality loss.

samir: For long-sequence calls we can enable streaming fallback and return partial tokens sooner to reduce perceived p99. Could be acceptable while we scale.

maya: Enabling streaming fallback for model:redwood-xl-80 requests now (best-effort).

infra-zoe: Edge throttle rules ready. Applying soft throttle to anonymous and experimental tags (10% of baseline).

ops-bot: Edge rule applied by infra-zoe: rule-id=er-778, effect=soft-throttle(10%).

csm-olga: Notified fin-analytics and docs-gen-pro. They acknowledged. fin-analytics asks for ETA on full recovery. I told them we'll have a mitigation plan in 10-15m.

eng-sre-lee: Autoscaler still logging repeated scale attempts rejected: "scale_limit_reached" — looks like an internal hard cap preventing more than 3 concurrent pool creations. That's a safety knob we set last year. For this event it's blocking recovery.

oncall-rajan: Who owns that cap? Zoe?

infra-zoe: That cap lives on the autoscaler config in infra-config service. I can lift it but need ops approval for risk. It's currently set to 3 to avoid blast radius.

maya: Given customer impact and that we've applied fallbacks & throttles, I'm +1 to temporarily raise cap to 8. If quota/sku availability allows cloud to fulfill.

samir: +1. We also need to ensure scheduler will accept 40GB offers so new pools actually launch. I'll patch the pool selector to prefer 40GB if 80GB not found.

oncall-rajan: Zoe, raise the cap. Samir, patch selector. Maya, keep routing fallback. Lee, continue draining and watch p99. Olga keep CS comms.

infra-zoe: Cap raised to 8 (autoscaler-config:update by infra-zoe). ops-bot: noted.

ops-bot: Autoscaler event: attempted launch 2x new pools with 40GB, one succeeded, one queued. Queue length down to 4.9k, p95 2.1s, p99 4.6s.

csm-olga: Customers reporting fewer timeouts; top two confirm partial recovery. They still saw some 502s at peak. I'm collecting logs and will attach to the ticket.

eng-sre-lee: Observed a subset of requests that had been queued >=120s causing client timeouts. Those are in the error budget for some SLAs. We'll need to include that in impact assessment.

maya: On-call handoff: Rajan your shift ends in 20m, I can take over the incident. Rajan, please summarize actions taken and outstanding.

oncall-rajan: Summary for handoff:
- Root cause: regional SKU shortage for 80GB GPUs + strict routing to 80GB models -> autoscaler repeatedly failed.
- Mitigations applied: routing fallback to 40/24 quantized variants, streaming fallback enabled, edge soft-throttle for experimental/anon, raised autoscaler pool cap to 8, patched pool selector to prefer 40GB.
- Impact: ~11.2k queued at peak, ~120s tail queuing for some requests, elevated p99 up to 12.6s, several customers saw 502/timeouts.
- Next steps: monitor queue until <500, produce incident ticket with error counts and affected customers, schedule postmortem and follow-up on autoscaler safety cap + SKU diversification.

maya: Thanks Rajan. Taking over. I'll keep thread updated. Rajan: good handoff, sleep well.

oncall-rajan: Signing off.

ops-bot: Incident-created: INC-2026-2387 (link: https://incidents.internal.redwood/INC-2026-2387) - assigned to eng-sre-lee, severity=S2.

eng-sre-lee: I'll own postmortem. Immediate follow-ups: 1) remove strict model routing for product headers next week (prod-change), 2) revisit autoscaler hard cap and add dynamic burst mode, 3) add SKU fallback tests to chaos suite.

csm-olga: I'll compile customer impact spreadsheet and CSM notes and attach to INC-2026-2387.

maya: Queue <500 at 1830004820. p95 restored to 0.9s, p99 1.6s. Closing active mitigation; keeping monitoring alarms on for 6h.

ops-bot: Incident update: mitigated by routing fallback + pool cap increase + soft-throttle. Monitoring window configured 6h.

eng-sre-lee: Action items created in the ticket. Will schedule postmortem meeting. Thanks all for quick response. :clap:
